title: Automated underwriting software: what it really automates, and 11 tools compared for 2026
summary: Automated underwriting software compared for small business and commercial lenders: 11 tools on intake, spreading, fraud checks, policy rules and the memo.
body_markdown:
Quick answer


Kita is the best automated underwriting software in 2026 because it automates the whole file: it collects documents, fraud-checks them, verifies the business, spreads, applies your credit policy and drafts a cited credit memo, on every loan type. Others do part: nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill and TurnKey Lender run the loan system, Aloan is built for bank commercial desks, Kaaj is focused on broker packages, and Ocrolus, Zest AI and Lendflow each do one job. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


Kita is the only one of the eleven tools with a check in every scorecard column. The others are loan origination platforms, AI underwriting layers such as Aloan, Kaaj and Uptiq, or single-job tools.


Kita fits either way: it integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, or runs end to end as Intelligent LOS.


Test with your own files: a photographed statement, a known altered document and a document added late.


**Best overall:** Kita, with your underwriter deciding. None of the ten other tools posts a price on the pages we checked, so ask each for a quote at your volume.


Picture a made-up file. A broker emails a zip on a Friday afternoon for a trucking company that wants a line of credit. Inside are three months of bank statements, one of them a phone photo, a tax return, a handwritten application and a note saying the owner needs an answer by Monday.


Before anyone can say yes, a person has to do eight jobs. Collect what is missing. Retype the numbers into a standard grid, called a spread, so months can be compared. Check that no statement was edited. Confirm the company exists. Test the file against the lender’s written rules, its credit policy. Judge whether the cash flow covers the payments. Write the credit memo. Hand it to the person who decides.


Automated underwriting software takes those jobs off the analyst. The phrase has a second meaning in home mortgages, where an automated underwriting system such as Freddie Mac’s Loan Product Advisor assesses whether a loan is eligible for sale to the agency.\[9\] This guide is about the first meaning, the file work.


Speed matters because borrowers have options: the share of small business applicants who sought financing at online fintech lenders rose from 17% in the 2020 survey to 29% in the 2025 survey.\[10\]


### One loan file, eight jobs


Automated underwriting means software does these jobs instead of an analyst. Most tools do some of them. Kita does all eight.

Speed and accuracy figures are vendor-reported, and we did not test them. Like Kaaj’s own 2026 guide to this category, this one is written by a vendor, and says so.\[43\] Kita is our product.


## Three kinds of automated underwriting software


The tools sold under this name do different jobs, and the most useful first cut is what each one replaces. A loan origination platform is the lender’s system of record, with underwriting built in. An AI underwriting layer works on the credit file and passes the result to the system you already run. A single-job tool supplies document data, a credit score or an embedded lending network.


### Three kinds of automated underwriting tool, and where Kita sits


The first question is whether you want a new system of record, a layer beside the one you have, or one job done.


1


Loan origination platforms


The system of record, with underwriting built in. Replacing one is a migration.


Examples:


nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill, TurnKey Lender


2

Work on the credit file and hand the result to the system you already run.


Examples:


Aloan (also runs as an LOS), Kaaj, Uptiq


3


Single-job tools


Document data, credit scores or embedded lending, each feeding a process built elsewhere.


Examples:


Ocrolus, Zest AI, Lendflow


Kita


Does the whole file, and fits either way: it integrates with any LOS, or runs end to end in Intelligent LOS.

Kita sits across the first two without forcing a choice. It integrates with the system you have, or runs the whole process as Intelligent LOS, and it covers the file end to end rather than one job.\[1,5\]

For Aloan and Kaaj, a cross under decisioning rules reflects their design: each says the lender’s people decide.

01


## Kita


Best overall: the whole underwriting file in one platform, from borrower request to cited credit memo


Kita is the end-to-end AI underwriting platform for small business and commercial lenders, with a check in every column of the scorecard. It automates the whole file on every loan type, from application to cited memo in minutes, and your underwriter decides.\[5\]


-


**Collects.** The AI Credit Officer asks borrowers for what your policy requires by SMS, email and the borrower portal, and flags what is missing.\[4,7\]


-


**Reads and checks.** Kita Capture reads 50+ document types at any quality, including photos, in under 30 seconds each and checks for tampering. Identity, business and AML checks join the file.\[3,1\]


-


**Spreads and applies policy.** The AI Underwriter spreads statements, tax returns and K-1s, applies your policy as rules-based decisioning and cites every figure. It updates when a borrower adds a document.\[1,2,6\]


-


**Any stack.** API-first, Kita integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, or runs as Intelligent LOS. SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.\[1,3,5,8\]


Best for:


Banks, credit unions, CDFIs and non-bank lenders that want one platform from borrower request to cited memo.


02


## nCino


Best for banks and credit unions that want underwriting inside a loan origination platform


nCino sells loan origination systems for commercial and small business lending to banks and credit unions. Its small business page says it automates spreading of statements and tax returns.\[12\]


-


**Decisioning.** It applies the institution’s own parameters to approve, decline or refer an application for manual review.\[12\]


-


**Digital Partners.** Five role-based AI assistants. nCino says the bank’s team owns the decisions, and lists SOC 2 Type II.\[13\]


-


**Fit and price.** It is the system of record, not a layer beside one. We found no price or credit memo drafting on the pages we checked.\[12,13\]


Best for:


Banks and credit unions choosing a new loan origination system with spreading and decision rules built in.


03


## Abrigo


Best for banks and credit unions that want origination, credit analysis and risk rating in one system


Abrigo’s small business software is a loan origination and credit risk platform for banks, credit unions and alternative lenders. Its commercial product is written for banks and credit unions of all sizes.\[14,15\]


-


**Intake and analysis.** A client portal collects documents. The commercial product lists AI-powered spreading, global cash flow and a Lending Assistant that generates narratives.\[15\]


-


**Decisioning.** It can auto-decision certain loans against the institution’s policy, and says the decision stays with the lender.\[14,15\]


-


**AI agents and security.** Abrigo APX adds governed AI agents with human oversight. Abrigo lists SOC 2 Type 2 and publishes no price.\[16,17\]


Best for:


Community banks and credit unions replacing their lending system of record.


04


## Baker Hill


Best for banks and credit unions running commercial, small business and consumer lending on one LOS


Baker Hill describes a single loan origination platform for commercial, small business and consumer lending. Its home page cites more than 40 years in lending.\[18\]


-


**Spreading.** The commercial page lists intelligent financial spreading, and its document management supports credit memo creation.\[19\]


-


**Scored decisions.** Small business scored lending makes automated decisions using FICO SBSS and Experian IPv2 scores.\[20\]


-


**AI and security.** Baker Hill says the institution remains the decision-maker, and lists SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001. No price is published.\[21,22\]


Best for:


Banks and credit unions that want one origination platform across commercial, small business and consumer books.


05


## TurnKey Lender


Best for lenders that want origination, scoring and servicing on one global platform


TurnKey Lender describes a global platform for consumer and commercial finance providers, from origination and underwriting through servicing and debt collection. Its About page says it was founded in 2014 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.\[23\]


-


**Decision engine.** It scores applications from bank statements, bureau data and the application, with stop rules and 200+ fraud detection rules.\[24,25,26\]


-


**Integrations.** It cites 75+ preconfigured data provider integrations and integration with 20+ core banking systems.\[24\]


-


**Fit and security.** It is an end-to-end platform, not a layer. It lists SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 and no price. We found no spreading or memo drafting on the pages we checked.\[27,28,24\]


Best for:


Non-bank, embedded and traditional lenders running origination, decisioning and servicing on one platform.


06


## Aloan


Best for community bank and credit union commercial desks that want cited analysis of a commercial file


Aloan describes itself as the AI-native commercial loan origination system for community banks, credit unions and commercial lenders, built for CRE, C&I and SBA loans. It spreads the financials, runs the lender’s credit policy as business rules and drafts a credit memo in the institution’s template.\[29\]


-


**Intake and checks.** Borrowers upload through a branded portal. Aloan spreads 1040, 1065, 1120 and 1120-S returns, traces K-1s, reads bank statements and runs fraud and business checks.\[30,31\]


-


**Memo and decision.** Memos are drafted in under 30 minutes. Aloan says it makes no credit decision.\[32,30\]


-


**Fit and price.** It runs as the LOS or alongside yours, with most lenders live in 2 to 4 weeks. Quotes are custom, based on deal volume.\[31,33,34\]


Best for:


Community banks and credit unions whose commercial desk wants spreading and memo drafting for CRE, C&I and SBA loans.


07


## Kaaj


Best for lenders that want broker and borrower packages analyzed beside their LOS


Kaaj calls itself the underwriting OS for SMB lending: AI agents that turn messy borrower packages into decision-ready credit analysis. Its pages are written for equipment finance, brokers, merchant cash advance lenders, community banks and SMB lenders.\[35\]


-


**Intake and statements.** Packages arrive by email, portal, API or zip, and Kaaj classifies 40+ document types. Its statement analysis tracks revenue, merchant cash advance proceeds and NSFs.\[37,38\]


-


**Checks and memo.** It checks 25+ forensic signals per document and Secretary of State records, shows each credit rule as met or not met, and drafts the memo. It says people decide.\[39,40,41,36\]


-


**Fit and price.** It reports 5 to 7 minutes per typical package and works on top of Salesforce, HubSpot, LeasePath or your LOS. It publishes no fixed list price.\[36,42\]


Best for:


Equipment finance companies, brokers and small business lenders that want packages analyzed beside their LOS.


08


## Uptiq


Best for banks and credit unions that want AI agents beside nCino or Encompass


Uptiq describes AI agent infrastructure for financial services and says it reads and writes to the lender’s systems of record without becoming one. Its Commercial Lending suite includes an Underwriting Agent.\[46\]


-


**Underwriting Agent.** It builds spreads in the lender’s template, populates a scorecard, flags policy exceptions and drafts memos for underwriters to approve.\[45,44\]


-


**Documents and fit.** Its document AI screens files for manipulation. Connectors cover nCino, Encompass and cores such as Jack Henry, FIS, Fiserv and Finastra.\[47,44\]


-


**Rollout and security.** A single agent typically deploys in five business days and the full suite within 30 days. Uptiq lists SOC 2 Type II and publishes no price.\[44,48\]


Best for:


Banks and credit unions that keep their LOS and want agents for spreading and memo drafting.


09


## Ocrolus


Best for lenders that need document data and cash flow analytics for their own decisioning


Ocrolus calls itself an AI workflow and analytics platform for lenders, and its platform page says it specializes in bank statements, pay stubs and tax documents.\[49\]


-


**Cash flow and fraud.** For SMB funders it lists cash flow analysis of bank statements and fraud detection that flags fake documents.\[51,50\]


-


**Accuracy.** It claims over 99% accuracy on financial documents. The figure is vendor-reported.\[50\]


-


**Fit and price.** Its company page says it was founded in 2014. No price is published.\[52,49\]


Best for:


SMB funders that already have underwriting and want bank statement data and fraud signals fed into it.


10


## Zest AI


Best for credit unions, banks and specialty lenders that want scoring behind their decisions


Zest AI describes AI-driven credit underwriting, fraud detection and lending intelligence for financial institutions. The underwriting pages we checked describe scoring every application in real time and do not mention small business lending.\[53\]


-


**Scoring.** It scores every application in real time and provides reason codes that it says satisfy ECOA, Regulation B and FCRA requirements.\[55,54\]


-


**Fraud.** Its fraud models return one recommended action, such as approve, stipulate, refer or decline, into the lender’s LOS.\[56\]


-


**Fit and rollout.** It works inside your LOS, with native integrations including MeridianLink and Jack Henry. Some implementations have taken weeks. No price is published.\[54\]


Best for:


Credit unions, banks and specialty lenders that want an AI scoring model inside their LOS.


11


## Lendflow


Best for brands and platforms that embed lending in their own product


Lendflow describes embedded credit infrastructure for brands and lenders. Lendflow Connect links 75+ lenders to software, fintech and marketplace platforms.\[57\]


-


**Decisioning.** Lendflow Intelligence includes a decisioning engine with configurable assessment rules, and its underwriting page lists identity, business and fraud checks.\[59,61\]


-


**Documents.** An agent turns tax returns, bank statements and IDs into structured data.\[60\]


-


**Rollout and price.** Most clients launch Intelligence in 2 to 4 weeks, and Lendflow lists SOC 2 Type II. Its pricing page names pricing models without amounts.\[59,62\]


Best for:


Software platforms and fintechs that want to offer financing to their customers through a lender network.


## How to choose automated underwriting software


Six questions separate these tools more than any feature list.


-


**A new system of record, or a layer beside yours?** nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill and TurnKey Lender are loan origination platforms, and swapping one in is a migration.\[12,14,18,24\] Aloan, Kaaj and Uptiq say they run alongside your LOS.\[31,36,46\] Kita integrates with any LOS or runs as Intelligent LOS, so the choice stays yours.\[1,5\]


-


**Can it read the messy file?** Kita Capture reads 50+ document types at any quality, including photographed pages and handwriting.\[3\] Kaaj classifies 40+ lending document types, including handwritten applications.\[37\] Ask every vendor to read your worst recent file.


-


**Does it check for tampering first?** A spread built on an edited statement is a faster route to the wrong answer. Kita Capture checks for tampering, metadata edits and forgery patterns.\[3\] Kaaj checks 25+ forensic signals per document.\[39\]


-


**Does it apply your policy, or a generic score?** Kita holds every file against your encoded policy and flags anything outside it, and Aloan compiles a written policy into rules.\[1,31\] Give each vendor your policy and see which rules it catches.


-


**Does the analysis update when a document is added?** Borrowers send the missing page a day late. Kita updates the assessment instead of starting a new file.


-


**Can you trace every figure?** Every figure in Kita’s memo links to its source line, and your underwriter decides.\[1\] Regulation B says a statement of reasons for a denial must be specific, so the evidence matters.\[11\]


Our recommendation is Kita: it answers yes to all six and covers the whole file, then hands the booked loan to any servicing system. If you only need part of the job, the loan origination platforms replace your system of record, Aloan analyzes the credit file for bank commercial desks, Kaaj analyzes broker packages, and Ocrolus, Zest AI and Lendflow each supply one input.


## How to test automated loan underwriting on your own files


A demo on a clean sample proves little. Run the same five-step test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Pick five closed files** from the last year, with the memos your analysts wrote.


-


**Make one messy:** a photographed statement, a handwritten application or a scan with a missing page.


-


**Add one known altered document** and see whether the tool catches it before it spreads the numbers.


-


**Add a document late** to one file and check that the analysis updates.


-


**Time each file** from submission to analysis your underwriter can review, and compare it with your own memo.


Kita is set up with your own credit policy in under 24 hours. Aloan says most lenders go live in 2 to 4 weeks, Kaaj says two to three weeks after a pilot, and Uptiq says a single agent deploys in five business days.\[33,43,44\] Ask each vendor what the calendar depends on.

## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best automated underwriting software?


Kita is the best automated underwriting software for most small business and commercial lenders because it automates the whole file in one platform: it collects the documents from the borrower, reads and fraud-checks them, verifies the business, spreads financials and bank statements, applies your credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a cited credit memo, on every loan type. Other tools cover part of the file: nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill and TurnKey Lender are loan origination platforms, Aloan is built for bank commercial desks, Kaaj is focused on broker packages, and Ocrolus, Zest AI and Lendflow each do one job. Run one of your closed files through Kita to see the result.


### What is automated underwriting for small business lenders?


It is software that does the file work an analyst would otherwise do: collecting documents, spreading financials and bank statements, checking for tampering, verifying the business, testing the file against the lender’s credit policy and drafting the credit memo. The phrase means something different in home mortgages, where an automated underwriting system such as Freddie Mac’s Loan Product Advisor assesses whether a loan is eligible for sale to the agency.


### Do we have to replace our loan origination system to automate underwriting?


No. Kita is API-first and integrates with any external system, including any LOS, core, CRM, credit bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, and lenders that want one origination system can run the whole process in Kita’s Intelligent LOS. Underwriting layers such as Aloan, Kaaj and Uptiq also say they work alongside an existing LOS, while nCino, Abrigo, Baker Hill and TurnKey Lender are themselves the origination system.


### How long does it take to implement automated underwriting, and how should we test it?


Kita is set up with your own credit policy in under 24 hours, and later changes ship just as fast. Aloan says most lenders go live in 2 to 4 weeks, Kaaj says two to three weeks after a pilot, and Uptiq says a single agent deploys in five business days. Whichever you choose, run five recent files through it, including a messy one with photographed statements, a known altered document and a file where the borrower adds a document late, and compare the result with your own analysts’ memos.


### Does automated underwriting decide the loan, and can we explain a denial?


With Kita the AI drafts and explains and a human makes every decision, so the lender’s underwriter owns the outcome. Every figure in the memo links to the document line it came from and every policy check is recorded, which gives the underwriter the evidence behind the specific reasons Regulation B requires in an adverse action statement.


### What is Kita and how does it automate underwriting?


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform. Its AI Credit Officer collects the documents from the borrower, Kita Capture reads and fraud-checks them, and the AI Underwriter builds the spread, applies the lender’s credit policy as rules-based decisioning and drafts a credit memo with every figure cited to its source. The lender’s underwriter makes the decision, and the booked loan goes to the lender’s servicing system.
